items.source: Sandisk 8-K exhibit 99.1, fiscal Q1 2027 results, Oct 29 2026
notes: Segments: Edge $5,832M (+320% Y/Y), Datacenter $4,802M (from $269M a year ago) and Consumer $397M (-39%), which foot exactly to $11,031M. Datacenter is the quarter: it was 12% of revenue a year ago and is 44% now, and it grew 61% sequentially on its own.

Revenue grew 378% year over year, from $2,308M. This is the NAND pricing cycle in its most extreme form -- cost of revenue rose only 2%, from $1,621M to $1,653M, while revenue grew almost fivefold. An 85% gross margin on a commodity memory business is a pricing artifact, not a structural one, and it reverses when pricing does.

NAND demand concern, as of Nov 2, 2026: the shares have fallen from $1,404.77 on Oct 28 to $1,075.08 on Nov 2, down 23% in three sessions, against this card's quarter being a record. The largest single day was a 13.5% fall on Oct 30, the day Kioxia reported. Kioxia's own quarter was also a record -- revenue of 2,480.0bn yen and operating profit of 1,994.7bn yen -- but it guided October-December adjusted operating profit to about 2.0tn yen against a consensus near 2.35tn, roughly 15% below, which implies NAND prices approximately flat quarter on quarter. Its average selling price rose in the mid-20% range in July-September against about 70% the quarter before. It gave no full-year forecast. Kioxia shares fell 15.8% in Tokyo on Nov 2 (source: Kioxia fiscal Q2 results of Oct 30, 2026, as reported by Investing.com and Seoul Economic Daily; prices from stockanalysis.com).

Kioxia is not a comparable -- it is Sandisk's manufacturing partner. The two co-own Flash Ventures, the three Japanese joint-venture entities (Flash Partners, Flash Alliance and Flash Forward) that supply ALL of Sandisk's flash wafers, 49.9% Sandisk and 50.1% Kioxia, extended in January 2026 through Dec 31, 2034. So Kioxia's read on NAND pricing is a read on the same wafers and the same cycle this card's 85% gross margin comes from (source: Sandisk FY2026 Form 10-K, sndk-20260703.htm; Kioxia and Sandisk joint announcement of Jan 29, 2026).

Broader semiconductor weakness is the layer underneath, and Oct 30 is where the two landed together. From the Oct 28 close to Nov 2: the Nasdaq-100 (QQQ) fell 6.1%, the semiconductor ETF SMH fell 10.5%, Sandisk fell 23.5%. SMH's worst session was Oct 30 at -6.98%, the same day Sandisk fell 13.5% -- driven largely by Intel, which guided fiscal Q4 revenue to $15.0-16.0bn against a consensus near $17.0bn and fell 28.6% in that session. So Sandisk's worst day was the sector day and the Kioxia day at once, which is why it is roughly double either on its own (source: Intel 8-K of Oct 29, 2026, q326earningsrelease.htm; prices from stockanalysis.com, read Nov 2, 2026).

Within that sector move, NAND is the worst-hit corner rather than the only one. Oct 28 close to Nov 2: NVIDIA -6.2%, QQQ -6.1%, SMH -10.5%, Micron -15.2%, Sandisk -23.5%, Intel -37.2%. Sandisk fell more than twice the semiconductor ETF, so the sector accounts for part of the move and NAND pricing for the rest; neither explains it alone. The cleanest read on the NAND-specific part is SK Hynix, which fell 7.1% on Oct 30 with everything else but ROSE 3.8% on Nov 2, the session Sandisk fell a further 6.6%. Micron and SK Hynix sell DRAM alongside NAND; Sandisk does not, and the absence of a second product line is the same concentration that produced 378% revenue growth on the upswing (source: stockanalysis.com, read Nov 2, 2026).

What the concern does and does not contradict: Sandisk's own guidance, given Oct 29, points the other way. CFO Luis Visoso said on the call that the company expects "pricing to continue to increase modestly throughout the year", and put fiscal Q1's growth at roughly 60% volume and 40% price. About 50% of fiscal 2027 bits and about two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits are committed under long-term agreements, 95% of them with investment-grade counterparties, which blunts a spot-price move without removing it. Supply cannot answer quickly either way -- Visoso put a wafer at "120 days or so" to produce, and the bit-growth plan stays mid-to-high teens. None of this revises the quarter the chart draws; it reprices the pricing assumption behind it (source: Sandisk fiscal Q1 2027 earnings call, Oct 29, 2026).

$513M of the $539M non-operating line is a gain on equity securities, not operating performance. Operating income of $8,780M is the figure that describes the business; net income of $8,101M is after that one-off gain and $1,218M of tax.
